svg.title: C23 / KEPLER METAL WORLDS engineering mission profile
svg.desc: C23, KEPLER METAL WORLDS. Original project: Investigating the Relationship Between Exoplanet Occurrence & Host Star Metallicity. Session C: Astronomy & Space Physics. Scientific question: How does occurrence in specified radius-period bins vary with metallicity after accounting for transit geometry, detection/vetting efficiency, reliability, and correlated host properties? Testable hypothesis: A selection-aware metallicity trend will depend on planet radius and orbital period; its uncertainty will increase when heterogeneous metallicity measurements and stellar-radius covariance are propagated.. svg.text: Investigating the Relationship Between Exoplanet Occurrence & Host Star Metallicity
No project observations acquired · specified cases await execution · shared demonstrations are separately labeled
Estimate planet occurrence as a function of host-star metallicity using a
defined survey target sample, candidates, completeness, and reliability.
Avoid comparing metallicity distributions of confirmed planets alone, which
lacks the denominator of searched stars. Separate planet size/period domains
and stellar populations so metallicity associations can inform formation
models without conflating transit detectability or stellar-parameter
How does occurrence in specified radius-period bins vary with metallicity
after accounting for transit geometry, detection/vetting efficiency,
TESTABLE HYPOTHESIS / NOT AN OBSERVED RESULT
A selection-aware metallicity trend will depend on planet radius and orbital
period; its uncertainty will increase when heterogeneous metallicity
measurements and stellar-radius covariance are propagated.
Restrict inference to a chosen Kepler sample with documented completeness
Multiplanet correlations and survey star selection are considered when
estimating errors and interpreting host trends.
VALIDITY LIMITS / THE CLAIM STOPS HERE
Metallicity samples may have their own selection function; photometric
metallicities can be imprecise. Trends in one transit survey do not
automatically transfer to direct imaging or radial-velocity domains.
COUNTS OF RECORDS · NO COMPLETION SCORES
TRACEABILITY / IDs THAT STAY WITH THE WORK
Execution evidence is required before case closure.
References are pointers; archive acquisition is separate.
A question becomes a model. A model earns evidence.
NASA-inspired mission names are creative identifiers. This profile describes research design; it claims no NASA approval or flight qualification.
Original titles are preserved. Data pointers and citations do not establish that the original teams’ observations have been acquired.
